title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the dictionary between oriented combinatorial maps and branched coverings of P^1(C) unramified outside {0,1,∞}, which later became the theory of dessins d'enfants. The previous page explains it: K is the inverse image of P^1(R), and the vertices of type i are the fibres over i. Ordinary maps correspond to ρ_1^2 = 1. In that case the map is the inverse image of [0,1], with vertices over 0, edge midpoints over 1 and face centres over ∞. The 'universal' oriented map (21) on P^1(C) is the segment K_∞=[0,1] with single vertex S_0={0}.

This page describes (22), its barycentric subdivision. It has S_1={1}, S_∞={∞} and K = P^1(R) = K_0 ∪ K_1 ∪ K_∞, with K_0=[1,∞], K_1=[∞,0], K_∞=[0,1]. The edge K_i, of type i, is opposite the vertex i. This is the universal oriented triangulated map: every 'subdivided' map is pulled back from it. Its two flag-triangles ('triangles-repères') are the upper and lower hemispheres r_+ and r_-. They are topological 2-simplices with common vertices 0,1,∞ and common edges K_0, K_1, K_∞.

The original map (21) has a single face. It is obtained by cutting the sphere along [0,1], giving a disk centred at ∞. The boundary is the single closed edge 0'(1/2)_- 1'(1/2)_+ 0', with one vertex 0'↦0 and 'midpoint' 1'↦1. The two boundary arcs from 0' to 1' pass through r_- and r_+ respectively.

Seen from ∞, the rays (∞,0') and (∞,1') divide the face disk into the two flags r_+ and r_-. r_+ carries the orientation induced by the face f; r_- carries the opposite one. These are the two flags of the single dart, i.e. the two flags exchanged by the barycentric involution. The margin notes fix conventions. The boundary orientation is the one induced from P^1(C). In the picture 0' ∞ 1' with r_+ on top, 0' must sit to the right of ∞ and 1' to the left.

Purpose: the next page uses the Riemann mapping theorem to find the conformal isomorphism g: D → f. It sends 0↦∞, 1↦0', -1↦1' and ±i↦(1/2)'_±. It is realised through the 'monogone' X_1 = P^1(C), a degree-2 cover of P^1 ramified over 0 and 1. In effect this is z ↦ -(z-1)^2/(4z), or its analogue with z^2. The aim is to make explicit the canonical conformal structure on the faces of a map, i.e. the cells of the dessin.
errors: Slip: '(contenant r_+)' should read '(contenant (1/2)_+)', parallel to '(contenant (1/2)_-)' for r_-.

Otherwise the combinatorics are correct: the edge K_i is opposite vertex i, and the two hemispheres are the two flags of the universal map. The orientation conventions are consistent with the figure and the margin note.

ideas.what: Universal oriented map on P^1(C): the segment [0,1] with vertex 0, edge midpoint 1, face centre ∞; every map is the pullback along a Belyi-type cover
ideas.modern_name: Universal (clean) dessin / universal map; Belyi pair correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme 1984); Jones–Singerman 1978 for the map/group side; Belyi 1979

ideas.what: Barycentric subdivision = triangulation of P^1 by P^1(R) into two hemispheres; flags (repères) = triangles of the subdivision, coloured 0,1,∞; orientation of a flag ± according to agreement with the face orientation
ideas.modern_name: Flag/barycentric triangulation of a map; black/white triangles of a dessin
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (implicitly, cartes et repères)

ideas.what: Cutting the sphere along the map to see the unique face as a disk centred at ∞, preparing a Riemann-mapping description of faces
ideas.modern_name: Canonical conformal structure on faces; equilateral/conformal realisation of dessins
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (canonical Riemann surface structure on a map)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard working-out of the universal dessin and its barycentric subdivision with orientation conventions. All of this is in the Esquisse and in the standard dessin literature.
transcription_corrections: '(contenant r_+)' in the manuscript is a slip for '(contenant (1/2)_+)'.
The annotation under K_∞=[0,1] in (22) reads 'comme avant cf (21)' and qualifies K_∞ only.
The phrase transcribed 'triangulaire pinceau' is doubtful; the handwriting looks more like 'triangulaire pré-galoisienne' or similar and should be flagged as uncertain.
Page number at the bottom is 62.
